vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: chainaware-behavioral-prediction
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle provides a legitimate integration with the ChainAware Behavioral Prediction MCP server for blockchain risk analysis. It includes well-defined tools for fraud detection, behavioral profiling, and rug pull detection, with clear instructions for the AI agent to handle API keys securely and obtain user consent before transmitting wallet addresses to the external endpoint (https://prediction.mcp.chainaware.ai/sse).

llm.summary: The skill's behavior (calling an external ChainAware MCP with wallet addresses using an API key) is coherent with its stated purpose, but there are metadata inconsistencies and a non-trivial privacy/exfiltration surface (wallet identifiers are sent to an external SSE endpoint) that you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to provide predictive on-chain fraud, behavior, and rug-pull detection and its SKILL.md requires an external ChainAware MCP API key and describes calls that send wallet and contract addresses plus network identifiers to a ChainAware SSE endpoint — this is coherent with the described purpose. However, registry metadata provided earlier indicated no required env vars or homepage while SKILL.md declares CHAINAWARE_API_KEY and gives a homepage; that mismatch is suspicious and should be resolved.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to send wallet addresses, smart contract/LP addresses and a network identifier to https://prediction.mcp.chainaware.ai/sse and to use CHAINAWARE_API_KEY as the apiKey parameter. It states that PII, raw tx data, and private keys are not sent. This instruction is within the skill's stated scope, but it does mean on-chain identifiers will be transmitted off-host to a third party — a privacy/consent consideration. The file also directs agent integration into various MCP-capable frameworks, increasing the chance of routine invocation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files, so nothing is written to disk or downloaded during install. That lowers installation risk compared with skills that fetch or run remote binaries.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md declares a single required environment variable (CHAINAWARE_API_KEY) as the primary credential, which is proportionate for an external API integration. However, the registry metadata provided with the skill (outside SKILL.md) indicated no required env vars — this inconsistency is concerning and could indicate out-of-date or tampered registry metadata. Also, although the SKILL.md promises the API key will never be logged or included in output, that is an instruction the agent must follow; the platform cannot independently enforce it — treat the API key as sensitive.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and uses the platform defaults (agent-invocable, may be called autonomously). This is typical for skills of this type and does not by itself increase privilege beyond the expected ability to be invoked by the agent. The skill does not request modifications to other skills or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: 1) Confirm the declared requirements — SKILL.md requires CHAINAWARE_API_KEY but registry metadata shows none; ask the publisher to clarify and reconcile the metadata. 2) Understand data leaving your environment: the skill will send wallet addresses, contract addresses and a network identifier to an external SSE endpoint (ChainAware). If those addresses are sensitive for your use case, avoid sending them or get explicit user consent. 3) Treat the CHAINAWARE_API_KEY as sensitive: store it securely, scope/restrict it where possible, and be prepared to rotate it if misused. 4) Review ChainAware's privacy policy and pricing, and verify the GitHub/homepage links and vendor identity before trusting predictions (claims like “~98% accuracy” should be independently validated). 5) If you need stronger guarantees, ask for a minimal test (non-sensitive addresses) and confirm the agent does not leak the API key or other secrets in outputs or logs. 6) If possible, reconcile the registry metadata discrepancy (no env vars) with the SKILL.md before deployment — mismatches like this reduce trust.
